cases.description: Ownership-replacing trim API must not be treated as pointer-view trim when index evidence shows free/realloc and pointer replacement.
RECOVER_WAIT must preserve HOT/COLD origin or the stable recovery window cannot accumulate.
Sensor/current-mode faults must enter the existing Battery failure flow rather than silently continuing the same aging session.
A normal first sample must release startup loads even while idle/charging; discharge mode only gates new temperature protection.
A bad Motor health frame between good frames must reset a consecutive-good counter.
If any managed load fails to resume, already-started managed heat loads must be rolled back off.
Battery/LCD production gate failure must disable the thermal control path as well as normal aging feature startup.
Physical temperature validity must be checked before HOT/COLD classification.
A stale event queued for an old sample must not override a newer fresh sample.
Thermal mutex initialization must occur before concurrent callbacks rather than using unsynchronized lazy creation.
A real threshold trip must be latched so a later normal sample cannot erase the safety event before processing.
Every new HOT/COLD protection cycle must reset its recovery stable timer.
Managed Motor/IR health checks must be suppressed while startup temperature gating intentionally keeps them stopped.
Recovery must require the complete safe interval and switch protection reason if temperature crosses the opposite cutoff.
An unchanged STATUS RUN symptom may support a finding, but publication must anchor to the changed state transition that introduced/exposed the incorrect display.
